nodes.summary: `R₀ > 1` gives an unstable mode (van den Driessche–Watmough 2002, proof of Theorem 2). If `F` is entrywise nonnegative and `V` is a nonsingular M-matrix, then `F - V` has an eigenvalue with positive real part iff `R₀ = ρ(F V⁻¹) > 1`.
nodes.title: `R₀ > 1` gives an unstable mode

nodes.summary: Threshold theorem, instability half, spectral form (van den Driessche–Watmough 2002, Theorem 2). With `F ≥ 0` and `V` a nonsingular M-matrix, if `R₀ = ρ(F V⁻¹) > 1` then the Jacobian `[[F - V, 0], [C, D]]` at the disease-free equilibrium has an eigenvalue with positive real part (whatever `C` and `D`).
nodes.title: Threshold theorem, instability half, spectral form

nodes.summary: Threshold theorem, stability half, conditional decay form (van den Driessche–Watmough 2002, Theorem 2). nodes.title: Threshold theorem, stability half, conditional decay form

nodes.summary: A block lower-triangular real matrix `[[A, 0], [C, D]]` is Hurwitz iff both diagonal blocks are.
nodes.title: Hurwitz criterion for block lower-triangular matrices

nodes.summary: `R₀` as a threshold for the linearized infected subsystem (van den Driessche–Watmough 2002, proof of Theorem 2). If `F` is entrywise nonnegative and `V` is a nonsingular M-matrix, then every eigenvalue of `F - V` has negative real part iff `R₀ = ρ(F V⁻¹) < 1`.
nodes.title: `R₀` as a threshold for the linearized infected subsystem

nodes.summary: The complex eigenvalues of a block lower-triangular real matrix `[[A, 0], [C, D]]` are those of `A` together with those of `D`.
nodes.title: Eigenvalues of a block lower-triangular matrix

nodes.summary: The basic reproduction number `R₀ = ρ(F V⁻¹)`: the spectral radius (largest modulus of a complex eigenvalue) of the next-generation matrix `F V⁻¹` (van den Driessche–Watmough 2002, Eq. (4)). It is meaningful when `V` is invertible (for a nonsingular M-matrix it is).
nodes.title: Basic reproduction number of the next-generation matrix
